This paper presents an overview of solar integration in buildings, with a specific focus on the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and compares the traditional Microgrid (MG) concept with a proposed innovative architecture. The proposed architecture incorporates the concept of Nanogrids (NGs) within a larger MG system, enabling decentralized energy generation and sharing. The Artificial Intelligence approach facilitates optimized energy distribution, load management, and efficient utilization of renewable energy sources. Additionally, Building-to-Building Renewable Energy Sharing (B2B RES) is explored as a potential solution to enhance energy utilization and efficiency. The proposed MG architecture and energy management approach offer a promising solution to achieve a sustainable and balanced energy system.

articleTitle: A Hybrid PV Power Forecasting Model Implementing Emerging Machine Learning Algorithms: Prophet and Neural Prophet
publicationTitle: 2023 Middle East and North Africa Solar Conference (MENA-SC)
abstract: To limit the dependency on non-regenerative energy, power utilities around the world are actively integrating photovoltaic technologies with existing electrical grids. Through this integration, a new generation profile is introduced to the existing supply profile, which imbalances the supply-demand of electric loads. Another noteworthy constraint is the dependency of the PV power generation on intermittent meteorological conditions, which profoundly impacts the continuity and quality of the generation. To address the raised constraints, the electricity generation profile demands thorough analysis to ensure stability of electrical grids. From this perspective, this paper proposes forecasting the PV power output for a short-term duration to overcome the constraints. Seven years (2014–2020) of historical data for a power plant in the United Arab Emirates were used to generate the forecasts. A hybrid forecasting approach was implemented, combining the emerging machine learning algorithms Prophet and Neural Prophet. Three univariate meteorological submodels (temperature, global irradiance, humidity) were built individually using the Neural Prophet algorithm. The power forecasting model was built using the Prophet algorithm, which utilized the meteorological forecasts and historical power readings. The results of the forecasts indicated good performance compared to the individual Prophet model.

articleTitle: Assessment of Cooling Effectiveness in Power Yields of a Multi-Orientational BIPV Façade of a High-Rise Building in a Hot and Arid Region: The Octagonal Tower
publicationTitle: 2023 Middle East and North Africa Solar Conference (MENA-SC)
abstract: The study presented in this paper is a multi-simulation of a project created by the author called “The Octagonal Tower,” an imaginary Office/Hotel tower in Dubai with façades facing eight orientations. The research objectives are to determine the energy yields and power generation of the BIPV system installed to each façade orientation and evaluate the losses due to increasing modules' temperature and the electric power gains from simulating different cooling levels for the BIPV systems. The reasoning of this analysis is due to the difference in the direct and diffused irradiance levels for each orientation at different times of the day, seasonal changes, as well as the different incidence angles and sun path. The different times each orientation receives the solar irradiance combined with the ambient temperature, wind speed, and other meteorological conditions significantly affect the power output and the modules' temperatures. The results assessed the arrays' temperature, power yields, and cooling effectiveness in the power gains for each façade orientation. Each orientation has its unique thermal behavior, which is important for identifying the cooling requirements compared with the potential gains. The average total gain of (13.86 %) was achieved by simulating cooling, with the South/West (17.7 %) at the highest gains, followed by South/East (17.3 %), and last is the North (3.9%). In three months, the North orientation and sub-orientations achieved higher power generation than the South. The South/East and South/West have higher power yields than the South. Cooling management of BIPV in summer is much more applicable than in winter; this will be described in the findings of this study.
